title: Person edits auto-enroll linked accounts; only HUMAN actors trigger it
answers: Why did an account become enrolled after someone assigned an AE or CSM?
Why does a workflow or AI tool get refused writing AE/CSM on an account?
How do accounts get enrolled in customer analytics ownership without running adopt_account_ownership?
body:
A person's assign / end_active / end_relationship on a controlled relationship enrolls the account under EVERY controlled definition (not just the edited one), in the same transaction, before the change's own activity row.
- Enforced in products/customer_analytics/backend/logic/relationships.py:_enroll_on_human_edit, called at the top of assign, end_active and end_relationship; body shared via _enroll_locked (also used by enroll).
- Trigger is actor.source == AccountRelationshipSource.HUMAN only. Workflow, AI tool, MCP, migration and Salesforce claim never enroll.
- Accounts with no external_id stay unenrolled; the link is read only under the account lock.
- Once enrolled, autonomous writers are refused on that role, so tests that need legacy/unmanaged holders must create them via a non-human actor (see test_account_ownership_commands.py:_assign).
applies: products/customer_analytics account relationship writes (logic/relationships.py) and tests that seed holders

search: Person edits (assign, end_active, end_relationship) on controlled relationships auto-enroll the account under all controlled definitions, but only when actor.source equals AccountRelationshipSource.HUMAN. Non-human actors (Workflow, AI tool, MCP, migration, Salesforce) never trigger enrollment. Enrollment happens in _enroll_on_human_edit at the top of these functions before the change's activity row; the logic is shared with _enroll_locked. Accounts with no external_id remain unenrolled. Once enrolled, autonomous writers are refused on that role. Tests requiring legacy/unmanaged holders must create them via a non-human actor call (see test_account_ownership_commands.py:_assign pattern). Applies to customer_analytics account relationship writes in logic/relationships.py and tests seeding account relationship state.
